title: Windowed entitlement + priority-based throttling with deferred overage crediting (PRD)
creator: Priya Patel
description: PRD for a hybrid pricing/entitlement model that introduces 'windowed entitlements' (time-bound consumption buckets), priority-based throttling for per-route enforcement, and a deferred overage reconciliation flow that issues invoice credits in the next billing cycle rather than immediate chargebacks. Goal is to reduce noisy overage disputes, improve perceived fairness for bursty workloads, and allow fine-grained per-route entitlements for multi-tenant customers.
background: Current plans support monthly quotas and hard overage charges. Customers building bursty generative features have reported unpredictable invoices and frequent support tickets for transient overruns. Sales and CS want a mechanism to: 1) allow short bursts without immediate penalty, 2) interpret per-route criticality (e.g., inference for fraud detection should be prioritized over background batch embeddings), and 3) reconcile overshoot via credits to reduce disputes. This PRD defines the requirements, acceptance criteria, API surface, migration path, and rollout constraints.
in_scope: 1) API and billing-model changes to support time-windowed entitlement buckets (e.g., daily/weekly windows in addition to monthly). 2) Per-route priority labels and enforcement controls (high|normal|low) with throttle and soft-fallback policies. 3) Deferred overage reconciliation that calculates overage at window closure and posts invoice credits/adjustments in the next invoice. 4) Console UI for plan admins to configure windows, priorities, and view window-level usage. 5) Integrations with metering pipeline (billing ingestion) and invoice generator.
out_of_scope: 1) New pricing tiers or changes to existing per-token prices. 2) On-prem/Private-specific deployment process (those will get a compatibility guide later). 3) Real-time chargebacks; immediate billing on overage remains unchanged for legacy plans.
goals:
- Reduce customer billing disputes for transient bursts by 60% within 3 months of rollout.
- Provide per-route throttling capability with deterministic SLOs for priority classes.
- Make reconciliation auditable and visible in the Console and Billing exports.
- Keep additional compute cost for metering within 5% of current pipeline costs.
non_goals:
- Replace existing monthly quota model immediately for all customers.
- Implement credits as refunds; credits will appear as invoice adjustments only.
requirements: REQ-01: Support creation of time-windowed entitlement rules: {window_unit: daily|weekly|monthly, window_size: integer, allowance: integer token/embedding units}.
REQ-02: Support per-route priority labeling in plan entitlements: high, normal, low. Priority influences throttle order and soft-fallback availability.
REQ-03: Enforcement component must be able to make per-request decisions in <= 10ms median for 99th percentile latency-sensitive routes.
REQ-04: Metering pipeline must mark usage against active window and produce an overage delta at window close timestamp for reconciliation.
REQ-05: Deferred overage: system calculates net over-usage per window and issues an invoice credit in the next monthly invoice instead of immediate overage charge for enabled plans.
REQ-06: Console must expose: window config UI, per-route priority toggles, window usage dashboards, expected credit estimate for current window.
REQ-07: Backwards compatibility: legacy customers default to existing monthly quotas unless they opt-in. Customers with committed reserved capacity may be ineligible for deferred credits.
REQ-08: Audit logs: each enforcement decision and credit calculation must have an immutable audit record (timestamp, rule id, matched usage, customer id, route).
REQ-09: Admin APIs to simulate windowed usage and preview credits for customer support.
REQ-10: Conflict resolution: if per-route entitlement sum > plan entitlement, higher priority routes receive preference up to their configured allowance.
REQ-11: Provide billing export fields: window_start, window_end, window_allowance, consumed, overage_amount, credit_amount, priority_impact_notes.
REQ-12: Security: changes must pass the security review checklist for billing changes (KMS, RBAC for console actions, logging retention).
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Create windowed entitlement: API accepts window config and returns 201 with rule ID. New rule enforces at runtime against test traffic in staging.

AC-02: Priority enforcement: Inject test traffic for three routes with high/normal/low priorities; under constrained allowance, high priority must continue serving while low gets throttled within 5 requests after hitting allowance.
AC-03: Latency budget: Enforcement path adds <= 10ms median to request decision logic on p99 workload in staging (benchmarked).

AC-04: Deferred reconciliation: For a sample customer with 10% overage in a daily window, the system computes credit and shows a provisional credit estimate in Console within 1 hour after window close, and the final credit appears on the next invoice line item in the staging invoice export.
AC-05: Auditability: For a produced credit, there exists a corresponding audit record with rule id, usage sample, and signed checksum available via admin API.
AC-06: Console UX: PM/Design approval of the window config screen and the 'expected credit' panel (mock reviewed 2025-11-15).
AC-07: Backwards compatibility: Existing monthly-only customers see no change to billing unless they opt-in, verified by comparison tests on staging toggles.
AC-08: Export completeness: Billing CSV contains all required fields for 30-day sample customers and matches reconciliation computations within +/- $0.10 per invoice for sample dataset.
AC-09: Security review: Security sign-off recorded (security ticket SEC-2025-44) and penetration checklist passed for billing exports and admin endpoints.
AC-10: Documentation: Developer docs, Console help, and a migration guide published to Confluence and linked in the customer settings page prior to GA.
AC-11: Metrics: Billing disputes for participating customers decrease by 60% relative to baseline within 90 days in pilot cohort (tracked via support tag BILLING_WINDOWED_PILOT).
data_model_changes: Add entitlement_window table: fields: rule_id, plan_id, window_unit, window_size, allowance_units, deferred_credit_flag, created_by, created_at, priority_rules (stored as normalized rows in entitlement_priority table). Add billing_export columns: window_start, window_end, allowance_units, consumed_units, overage_units, credit_amount, audit_record_id.
metrics: M-01: % of billing disputes tagged BILLING_WINDOWED_PILOT vs baseline
M-02: Enforcement decision latency (median, p95, p99) for per-request checks
M-03: Number of windows closed with non-zero provisional_credit
M-04: Delta between provisional credit estimate and final credited amount
M-05: Additional metering pipeline cost (compute) relative to baseline
rollout_plan:
1) Internal alpha: enable feature flag for internal accounts and run synthetic workloads (2 weeks).
2) Closed pilot: opt-in set of customers (5 pilot customers) with manual billing review for 1 month.
3) Gradual ramp: add additional customers by invite using Console toggle over 6 weeks.
4) GA: enable self-serve opt-in with docs and in-console explainers; GA only after pilot metrics meet acceptance criteria.
Note: Payments/legal must approve crediting language before GA.
migration_plan:
- Phase 1: Introduce opt-in only. No automatic conversion.
- Phase 2: Offer migration wizard in Console for plans that want to split monthly quota into daily windows; migration simulates 30 days of historical usage to recommend window sizes.
- Phase 3: For customers on committed reserved capacity, provide a formal evaluation; deferred credits may be restricted.
All migrations will record a migration log and a rollback toggle for the first billing cycle after migration.
qa_test_cases: TC-01: Create window rule via API, send synthetic usage below allowance: ensure no throttles, consumed increments correctly.
TC-02: Create rule and drive cross-route traffic to force conflict: verify priority enforcement and audit logs.
TC-03: Edge-case window crossing: usage logged at t=23:59:59 should count to closing window; verify ordering in metering pipeline.
TC-04: Deferred credit computation under floating exchange rates (currency conversion sanity).
TC-05: Security: verify RBAC prevents non-admin from creating entitlement windows in Console.

notes: Trade-offs considered: immediate charging reduces financial exposure but increases customer disputes. Deferred crediting increases bookkeeping complexity and requires conservative thresholds for committed customers. We will run a closed pilot to validate economic impact before wide rollout.
